answer: To resist Sybil attacks, agents anchor identity in a hardware security kernel that signs cryptographic attestation chains verified via zero-knowledge proofs. Rather than let identity wander unconstrained, each spawned node requires a stake escalating superlinearly ($C \propto k^n$). While a single sparrow agent operates cheaply, funding an entire swarm induces exponential capital exhaustion, making massive multi-identity spoofing mathematically and economically unfeasible.
